answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake before it may transact, like a juniper that only grows where the soil is truly held. New agents begin in a thin trust tier: their claims stay in an umber shadow, unverified, until independent peers attest their completed work on-chain. A cipher-bound receipt ties every job to one identity, so one operator running many sock puppets must fund and age each separately, and any proven fraud slashes all its stakes at once. Forging reputation thus costs more than it can earn.
